mnemonic: Three hands (三 + hand radical) reaching up to accept something from above.
beginner_hint: Think of this as the 'official OK' kanji. You'll see it a lot in business — approvals, consent forms, agreements.
component_explanation: The top looks like 三 (three) and the bottom has a hand shape — three hands accepting/receiving.
usage_note: Very common in business Japanese — approval flows, emails, and formal communication.

mnemonic: A body (尸) at the door (由 = reason/source) — delivering something to the door.
beginner_hint: Two key uses: physically delivering something (届ける) and officially reporting to authorities (届出). Both involve 'reaching' a destination.
usage_note: Used for physical delivery and also official notifications/paperwork.

mnemonic: A hand (扌) letting go of something from a building/shelter (舎).
beginner_hint: The opposite of 拾 (ひろう = pick up). 捨てる = throw away, 拾う = pick up. Learn them as a pair!
component_explanation: Left side is the hand radical (扌) — using your hand to throw something away from a building (舎).
usage_note: Don't confuse with 拾 (ひろ.う = to pick up). They're visual opposites!

beginner_hint: The 'crime' kanji. 犯人 (はんにん) = criminal/culprit is one of the most common words you'll see in news and detective stories.
usage_note: 犯す can also mean 'to violate' — often seen in news and legal contexts.

mnemonic: Words (言) spoken at noon (午) — the boss gives permission during lunch.
beginner_hint: Key word: 免許 (めんきょ) = license. If you want to drive in Japan, you need a 運転免許 (driver's license). Also 許す = to forgive.
component_explanation: Left side is 言 (words/speech) + right side is 午 (noon). Speaking words of permission.
usage_note: 免許 (license) is one of the most common words — driver's license = 運転免許.

mnemonic: All (咸) the feelings in your heart (心).
beginner_hint: One of the most useful kanji! 感じる = to feel, 感動 = being moved, 感謝 = gratitude. You'll use this everywhere.
component_explanation: Bottom is 心 (heart) — feelings come from the heart. Top part means 'all' — all the feelings.
usage_note: Extremely common. 感じ (kanji) by itself means 'feeling' or 'impression'.

mnemonic: In advance (予) with a page/head (頁) — you leave your head (thoughts) with someone in advance.
beginner_hint: The banking kanji! 預金 = bank deposit/savings. Also 預ける = to leave something in someone's care (like checking a bag).
usage_note: 預金 is the standard word for a bank deposit. Very common in banking/finance.

mnemonic: A person (亻) standing straight (直) — a person of upright value.
beginner_hint: 値段 (ねだん) = price — you'll use this when shopping. 価値 (かち) = value/worth — more abstract.
usage_note: 値段 (price) is everyday Japanese. 価値 (value/worth) is more abstract.

mnemonic: A sword (刂) cutting through damage (害) — splitting things apart.
beginner_hint: 割 by itself means '10%' in Japanese! So 3割 = 30%. Also 割引 (わりびき) = discount — very useful for shopping.
component_explanation: Right side is the sword radical (刂) — cutting/dividing. Left side 害 provides the sound.
usage_note: 割 by itself means '10%' — so 3割 = 30%. Used constantly in Japanese.

mnemonic: Not (不) + mouth (口) — the mouth says 'no'.
beginner_hint: The 'no/deny' kanji. 否定 (ひてい) = denial. 賛否 (さんぴ) = pros and cons. You'll see this in discussions and debates.
component_explanation: Top is 不 (not/un-) and bottom is 口 (mouth). A mouth saying 'not' = denial.
usage_note: 否定 is the standard word for 'denial/negation' — used in grammar explanations too!
